# Texture Splatting

Also called: Textured Splat Rendering, Texture Splatting for Scalar Fields, Wang's Texture Splatting on Particles

## Overview
Texture Splatting is a volume rendering technique that represents volumetric data or point clouds as a set of texture-mapped primitives (typically quads or squares) rasterized onto the screen [G]. It solves the problem of rendering high-frequency detail and complex scalar/vector fields efficiently by offloading the reconstruction kernel evaluation to the fragment shader via texture lookups, rather than computing per-fragment kernel values analytically [G]. It sets itself apart from standard Gaussian Splatting [9438-gsplat.md] by using texture maps to store color, normal, or other per-fragment properties, allowing for higher fidelity with fewer primitives and avoiding the artifacts associated with polygonal mesh approximations of Gaussian kernels [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
Builds on the shared splatting mechanism defined in [Splatting](23-splatting.md) [G].

## Subtopics

### [Textured Splat Rendering](14075-textured-splat-rendering.md)
Textured Splat Rendering is a point cloud visualization technique that renders each point as an oriented quad, computing per-fragment texture coordinates in the fragment shader to retrieve high-frequency color and normal data. It solves the detail loss inherent in standard scaled splats by decoupling geometry storage from color storage, allowing for aggressive pruning of the point cloud while maintaining visual fidelity. Unlike flat splats where properties are constant across the primitive, this method recovers high-frequency detail with fewer samples and larger radii. See [Textured Splat Rendering](14075-textured-splat-rendering.md).

### Texture Splatting for Scalar Fields
Texture Splatting for Scalar Fields is a volume rendering technique using texture-mapped squares to represent scalar fields, utilizing an ideal reconstruction kernel to improve image quality over polygonal approximations [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from Gaussian splats by being faster when splats are small, because rendering one texture-mapped square is cheaper than rendering a Gouraud-shaded triangle strip of ten triangles, though Gaussian splats become faster as screen-space coverage increases [S1, unofficial]. It is chosen for visualizing scalar fields where small splat coverage is dominant. A splat size of 1.6 results in sixty percent overlap between adjacent splats [S1, unofficial]. Polygonal mesh approximations (e.g., using radial and azimuth samples) exhibit visible artifacts and rapid cutoff of the Gaussian function, which texture splats avoid [S1, unofficial].

### Wang's Texture Splatting on Particles
Wang's Texture Splatting on Particles is an extension of texture splatting on particles to model about a dozen types of clouds with artistic control [S2]. It sets itself apart by texturing particles differently depending on the target cloud type [S2]. It is chosen for artistic cloud rendering.

## Background
Texture Splatting originated as a technique to render large datasets efficiently by leveraging texture hardware [G]. Westin et al. introduced texture splats for 3D vector and scalar field visualization, demonstrating the use of ideal reconstruction kernels to avoid polygonal artifacts [S1, unofficial]. Wang extended these concepts to cloud modeling, allowing for artistic control over different cloud types by texturing particles differently [S2].

## Sources
